task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
I found your account, and I've identified the likely cause of the problem.

**Line 555-123-2002 (your line):**
- Status: Active
- Plan: Premium Plan (15 GB data limit)
- Current cycle usage: **15.1 GB of 15.0 GB** — you've exceeded your plan's data limit

When a line's data usage exceeds the plan limit, data connectivity is lost or severely slowed, which matches what you're describing. Your account otherwise looks fine — no overdue bills, and the line is active and in contract (through 2026-12-31).

I have two options to restore your data:

**Option 1 — Refuel data (this billing cycle)**
- Adds data to your line immediately, at **$2.00 per GB** per your Premium Plan's refueling rate.

Which would you prefer? If you'd like to refuel, just let me know how many GB (up to 2 GB) you'd like me to add.

turns.thought:
Thanks for checking that — there are three separate things in your status bar that would each cause exactly the slow/no-data problem you're having. Let's work through them one at a time so I can confirm each fix before moving on.

**1. Mobile data is turned OFF ("Data Disabled")**
This is the most likely reason data stops working entirely. Even though we've refueled your plan, the phone's main mobile-data switch is off, so it won't use the cellular network at all.

Please do this on your phone:
- Open **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections**
- Turn **Mobile Data** **ON**

Tell me once that's done and let me know what the status bar shows (signal, network type, data status). Once mobile data is on, I'll walk you through the next fix — the phone is currently latched onto **2G**, which would keep speeds extremely slow even with data enabled.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn mobile data on.

turns.thought:
Good work — data is enabled now, so that fix took. Let's take the next one.

**2. The phone is set to prefer 2G**
Your status bar shows "2G". That's an old network technology that will keep your data painfully slow even though data is now on. Let's switch it to prefer the fast networks:

Please do this on your phone:
- Open **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Mobile Network**
- Tap **Network mode / Preferred network mode** (sometimes under "Advanced")
- Select **5G/4G preferred** (or "LTE/5G auto")

Tell me once that's done and let me know what the status bar shows. I expect the network type to change from "2G" to 4G/LTE or 5G — I'll confirm it with you before we move on.

After that we still have two more to clear: the **Data Saver** icon (which throttles data in the background and makes things feel sluggish) and the **VPN** connection (which can slow speeds significantly on its own).
turns.execution_output: User: Let me change the network mode.

turns.thought:
Excellent — that's a big improvement: you're now on **5G with four bars (excellent signal)** and data enabled. That alone should have made the connection much faster.

**3. Data Saver is ON**
The Data Saver icon restricts background data usage, which can make apps and services feel sluggish or unresponsive. Let's turn it off:

Please do this on your phone:
- Open **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Data usage**
- Tap **Data Saver** and turn it **OFF**

Let me know once that's done and read me the status bar again — I want to confirm the Data Saver icon is gone before we tackle the last item.

**4. VPN is connected (still pending)**
We'll deal with this after Data Saver. An active VPN can also slow your connection noticeably, so we'll check it once the above is confirmed.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me turn off Data Saver.

turns.thought:
Nice — Data Saver is cleared, and you're now on **5G with four bars (excellent signal), mobile data enabled**. All the throttling settings are resolved; the only item left is the VPN.

**4. VPN is connected (the remaining item)**
You mentioned a VPN connected icon. A VPN can be fine, but when it's slow or misconfigured it noticeably drags down mobile data speeds — and it's the one remaining variable that could still be affecting you.

Before I ask you to change anything with it, let's see where you actually stand now:

- Please try using your data right now — load a webpage, refresh an app, or stream a short video — and tell me how it feels (fine, fair, poor).
- Also, if you can, open your VPN app (or **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → VPN**) and tell me what it reports for the connection / performance level.

If your speeds are already good, you can simply leave the VPN on and we're done. If it still feels slow or the VPN reports a poor performance level, the next step would be to disconnect the VPN and re-test — I'll guide you through that and confirm the status bar afterwards.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check on both of those.

turns.thought:
That pins it down — the VPN is connected and reporting **poor** server performance, and it's routing all your traffic. A VPN with poor performance is a very common cause of exactly what you're seeing: full signal, 5G, data enabled, but no usable connection. Right now it's the last known thing standing between you and working data.

Please disconnect the VPN on your phone:
- Open **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → VPN**
- Tap the **gear/settings icon** next to the connected VPN, then tap **Disconnect** (or tap **Forget** if you don't plan to use it again)
- **Alternative if that's awkward:** pull down the quick settings shade and tap the **VPN / key icon** to turn it off. If your VPN app is installed (OpenVPN or similar), you can also just open it and tap **Disconnect**.

Once it's off, please:
1. Confirm the **VPN icon is gone** from your status bar.
2. Run the speed test again and tell me the result.

If data is restored with the VPN off, please reconnect your VPN only if you actually need it — and consider switching to a different server, since this one (192.168.1.1) is performing poorly and will reintroduce the problem whenever it's active. Let me know what you get.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me disconnect the VPN.

turns.thought:
I completely understand your frustration — three of the four settings issues are now fixed, and I've verified on my side that your line is **Active**, in contract through 2026-12-31, and that the **2 GB refuel is applied** (you have about 2 GB of headroom). So the problem is now almost certainly on the device side rather than the account side, and there are still two known causes left to rule out.

Let's take the next one:

**5. Check your SIM card status**

A SIM that isn't seated properly will cut off data even with a perfect signal — it's a common cause of "full bars but no connection."

Please do this:
- Open **Settings → About phone → Status** (or **Settings → Connections → SIM manager**, depending on your phone)
- Look for **SIM card status** and tell me exactly what it says

Then:
- **If it says "No SIM" / "Missing"** — please power the phone off, remove the SIM tray, reseat the SIM card firmly, reinsert it, and power back on. Then re-run the speed test.
- **If it says "Locked"** (asking for a PIN/PUK) — don't try entering codes. Tell me, and I'll get you to our SIM security team, since I can't unlock that from here.
- **If it says "Active" / "Ready"** — that rules out the SIM, and we move straight to the next step.

The step after this (if the SIM is fine) is your **APN settings** — that's the setting your phone uses to actually reach the carrier's data network, and an incorrect or blank APN produces exactly this "excellent signal, 5G, no connection" pattern. Resetting it to default and rebooting resolves it in most cases.

Let me know what the SIM status shows.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the SIM status.

turns.thought:
Good — SIM is "Active", so that's ruled out. That leaves the most likely remaining cause:

**6. Check your APN settings**

The APN (Access Point Name) is the setting your phone uses to actually reach the carrier's data network. When it's incorrect or has a missing/blank MMSC URL, you get exactly your symptom: excellent signal, 5G, data enabled — but "No Connection" on a speed test.

Please do this:
- Open **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Mobile Network → Access Point Names (APN)**
- Look at the entry that's selected (there's usually a dot/radio button next to the active one) and tell me:
  - Whether it shows **"Incorrect"** or any kind of warning
  - What it lists for **APN name**
  - What it lists for **MMSC** (this may be blank or show "Not set")

**What we'll do based on that:**
- If the APN shows **"Incorrect"**, or the **MMSC is blank / "Not set"**, I'll walk you through **resetting the APN to default**: open the **menu (⋮)** in the APN screen and tap **Reset to default**.
- **Important:** after resetting the APN, you must **reboot your device** for the change to take effect — a speed test before the reboot won't reflect it.

Once you've rebooted, run the speed test again and let me know the result. Tell me what the APN screen shows and we'll go from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check the APN settings.

turns.thought:
Thanks — that rules out the APN. Your APN name ("internet") and MMSC URL (`http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc`) are both correctly set with no warning, so that's not the cause either.

Just to confirm the account side is still clean: your line is **Active**, plus the **2 GB refuel is applied** (usage 15.1 GB against an effective 17 GB), so you have data available. The problem is now isolated to the device itself.

**7. Reboot your phone**

You've changed several settings in a row — mobile data, network mode to 5G, Data Saver, and the VPN disconnection. A full restart refreshes all your phone's network services and connections, and this is often what's needed for all those changes to settle in and for data to come back.

Please:
- Press and **hold the power button**, then tap **Restart** (or power off, wait ~30 seconds, then power back on)
- Wait for the phone to fully boot and reconnect — give it a minute or two
- Check the status bar, then **run the speed test again** and tell me the result

If the speed test comes back with an actual speed (even "fair"), we're done and your data is restored.

If it still reports **"No Connection"** after the reboot, I won't ask you to keep repeating steps — I'll escalate you directly to our technical support team so they can run deeper diagnostics on your line and device from their end. I'd rather do that than have you keep retrying things that aren't working.

Go ahead and reboot, and let me know what the speed test says.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me reboot the phone.

turns.thought: I'm sorry this has taken so many attempts without a result — I understand the frustration, and I'm going to hand you straight over now rather than have you repeat anything else.
